question.problem: A basketball player has a $70%$ chance of making a free throw on any given attempt. The player continues shooting free throws until they make a shot. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that the player will attempt fewer than $4$ free throws is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of free throws attempted until the player made a shot. Since the chance of making a free throw is $70%,$ the number of free throws attempted until the player makes a shot can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=70%=\frac{70}{100}=0.7.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.7).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.7)^{x-1}(0.7) \\  & =(0.3)^{x-1}(0.7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the player will attempt fewer than $4$ free throws is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(0.3)^{0}(0.7)+(0.3)^{1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{2}(0.7) \\  & =0.7+0.21+0.063 \\  & =0.973.\end{aligned}
$$
